pull.title: fix: recover cancelled publication PaymentIntent cleanup after restart
pull.body:
## Summary
- persist cancelled job-publication PaymentIntent cleanup work in PostgreSQL in the same transaction that commits local `CANCELLED`
- add Flyway V56 with cleanup attempt/lease/completion/review state and backfill historical cancelled publications
- claim cleanup work under pessimistic row lock, commit the short claim transaction, then call Stripe without holding a DB lock
- use a two-minute restart lease so a process crash before/after the provider call becomes retryable
- always re-read authoritative PaymentIntent state; a provider-side cancel followed by process crash is observed as `canceled` on retry instead of canceling twice
- add capped exponential retry and fail-closed review quarantine after repeated ambiguous failures
- keep late successful payment authoritative: cancelled publication stays cancelled, normal signed-webhook wallet settlement runs, cleanup becomes terminal
- add a separate scheduled recovery worker so cleanup missed by the immediate cancellation/expiry path is rediscovered after restart
- add scheduler, queue/state/race tests and architecture documentation

## Crash window closed
Previously local cancellation/refund could commit and the process could die before the one-shot `PaymentIntent.cancel()` call. The expiry scheduler would never select that row again because it was already `CANCELLED`, leaving an active Stripe PaymentIntent attached to a terminal publication.

Now provider cleanup is durable work. Crashes before the provider call, during the call, or after a successful provider cancel but before local completion all converge through lease expiry + authoritative provider re-read.

## Safety properties
- no DB transaction/row lock spans a Stripe network call
- competing app instances may see the same due id, but only one can claim it after locked re-check
- local wallet reservation restoration never depends on Stripe availability
- cleanup itself never moves wallet money
- a late payment never resurrects the cancelled publication
- successful cleanup clears the failure field; repeated unresolved failures are quarantined instead of spinning forever

## Migration
- V56 `job_publication_payment_intent_cleanup_recovery`

## Required validation before merge
- exact-head Maven/API verify including new unit tests
- Web audit/test/lint/build
- Production Compose contract
- full container/runtime smoke with Flyway V56 applied on real PostgreSQL
- exact-head mergeability + unchanged master verification

Merge only with a merge commit and exact expected head SHA after every check is completed and green.
